depth_proxy.rule: 10 % of the median volume traded before the T-24h cutoff per settled market

full_hedge_cost.note: hedge P&L minus the same contracts at mid (spread + fee) per day, observed run, uncapped hedge

deviations: D1 (2026-09-30T18:52:06Z, after the first full run at 18:50Z): under the frozen limits (mu_r +/- l*MAD_r, l <= 0.25, MAD ~0.5 wet days) a hedger's residual premium is under one tick of the 14-wide scalar ($0.14 per unit-week), so only 2-4 % of residual units fill and the primary two-leg book is almost the station leg alone. Added a residual 'absorb-all' sensitivity: the house takes every business's residual units (q_r = -sum h per cell, like Phase 4 D4(b)); capital, R3 ratio and junior reported for it alongside the primary. Also: clearing - fair is now averaged over markets that traded, and the no-trade share is reported (first run averaged over no-trade markets too). The primary rules and verdicts are unchanged.

lines.evaluation_s7_paragraph: Rain as a weekly two-leg book (wet-day cover; station leg = daily Kalshi rain binaries, residual = PRISM per-cell spread; `reports/eval-04-05/rain_book.json`). Almost nothing nets: 0.003 of units cancel (`netting.central.pooled`), because nearly every sector loses on wet days. At 2 % participation the pool is short $282k of payout per wet day across the five cities (`netting.leftover.<ST>.leftover_units_per_day`), and Kalshi's daily rain markets can absorb about 700 contracts a day against about 205,000 needed (`depth.by_city.<ST>.depth_proxy`, `.mean_net_short_contracts`; a volume proxy, no order-book history), so the house carries it. The 30-day capital is $1.08M on the 2024-26 window (`capital.two_leg_joint.H30.C`; Phase 4's heat book: $412k, `handoff.C30_usd`), 0.17 of 30-day notional (`R2.CPC`), and $1.47M for the station leg on 1999-2025 (`capital.station_long_1999_2025.H30.C`); the season (153-day) figure is $2.51M (`capital.two_leg_joint.H153.C`). The residual leg adds little capital: ×1.00 as priced (`R3.ratio`), ×1.08 if the house wrote every residual unit (`D1_absorb_all.ratio30`). With senior paid out of margin, the junior's median May-Sep season is +12 % and the 1-in-20 season -147 % (`junior.model_MaySep.splits.margin_t10`), so the three-season test fails (`R5.margin_t10`).
lines.memo_line: Rain cover doesn't net and Kalshi's daily rain markets are about 300 times too thin to lay it off, so a rain book is the pool's own risk: about $1.08M of 30-day capital at 2 % take-up, and the junior loses money in a bad year.
